svg.text: TASK MANAGEMENT — TASK LIFECYCLE & EVENT PATH
THE STATE MACHINE — the table lives on the TaskStatus enum
createTask
TODO
the ctor's default
pick it up
IN_PROGRESS
raise the PR
IN_REVIEW
approved
DONE
completedAt stamped
changes requested
BLOCKED
reachable from all three working states
unblocks back to TODO or IN_PROGRESS only
REOPEN — DONE → TODO is the ONLY exit from DONE, and it CLEARS completedAt
IN_PROGRESS → DONE throws IllegalStateException
you cannot skip review. The message even prints allowedNext(),
so the caller is told exactly what WAS legal.
A self-transition (X → X) is always allowed — a retried
PATCH is idempotent and fires NO event.
Every rule above is five EnumSets in a static block —
no switch, no per-state class, one readable table.
THE RACE — and why transitionTo returns the old value
BROKEN: old = task.getStatus(); task.setStatus(next); notify(old, next)
T1 and T2 both read TODO → both publish "TODO → IN_PROGRESS"
the activity feed now shows a history that never happened
FIXED: TaskStatus old = task.transitionTo(next); // synchronized
read-old, validate and write-new happen in ONE critical section
the loser's transition is either legal (and sequenced) or throws
the lock is the Task's own monitor → per-task granularity, no global lock
THE EVENT PATH — copy, then notify
1. if (old == new) return — no event for a no-op update
2. synchronized (observers) { copy = new ArrayList<>(observers); }
3. for (o : copy) o.onTaskStatusChanged(task, old, new) — lock released
a listener may register another listener mid-notify — no CME, no deadlock ✓
honest: still synchronous on the caller's thread — one throwing listener
aborts the rest of the fan-out and surfaces to whoever moved the task
THE QUERIES — honest about the O(n) scan
every query is the same shape
tasks.values().stream()
.filter(…)
.collect(toList())
byStatus · byAssignee · byPriority · byTag
createdBetween(start, end)
O(n) over EVERY task, every call
but ConcurrentHashMap iteration is weakly
consistent → never throws, never blocks writers
getOverdueTasks() — two predicates
dueDate != null
&& dueDate.isBefore(now)
&& status != DONE
the second clause is the one people forget:
a task finished late is NOT still overdue
null dueDate = "no deadline", never overdue
"was it delivered late?" is a different question —
that one reads completedAt vs dueDate
how I'd scale it
• secondary indexes maintained on write:
Map<assigneeId, Set<taskId>>, same for status/tag
• overdue: a priority queue keyed by dueDate,
so the answer is a prefix read, not a scan
• the cost: indexes and the map must move
together, which means a real lock per write
at board scale (hundreds of tasks) the scan wins —
say WHEN you'd add the index, not just that you could

g.text: ① Only transitions in allowedNext are possible.
② completedAt is set iff status == DONE.
③ One transition = at most one event.
④ A DONE task is never overdue.
